title: DOWNHILL BRAKE / GRAVITY RESPEND / CATCH RUNOUT

source.identity: Garfield (The Curse of Cleofatra) — Garfield: Caught in the Act — Sega Genesis — Playable Characters
observed: whole static sheet contains named Run, Slip, Edge, Fall, Push and jump/travel families
Push contrasts trustworthy contact with suppressed root translation; Slip contrasts visible contact with continued root travel
campaign artifact explicitly proposes downhill braking as next scene: friction trustworthy while gravity continuously re-spends root momentum after each catch

principle: TRUSTWORTHY BRAKES DO NOT END DOWNHILL MOTION WHEN THE FIELD RE-SPENDS MOMENTUM BETWEEN CATCHES.
quality_thesis: Each brake support must visibly acquire ahead of the moving root, survive root/COM passage through compression, then unload into a renewed spacing increase caused by downhill demand. The longest free catch arrives only after repeated re-spend. Corrections shorten and settle displaced.

rounds.basis: All 26 decoded frames and 13 authored states inspected. Each trusted brake point stays world-fixed across compression/overrun, spacing contracts during braking then re-expands after unloading, and the later 16px free catch is the largest displacement. Torso counter-lean and arm overshoot lag the root before a shorter displaced correction. Final CRF40 H.264 presentation was freshly decoded and inspected; encoding compression does not erase support ownership, root-spacing changes, counter-lean, or secondary lag.

noodle_queen.basis: The descending support teeth, repeated brake/re-spend sentence, asymmetric counter-lean and delayed arm debt read as one specific locomotion mechanism rather than a generic gait. The final compact encoding preserves the same readable silhouette/support sentence.
